concept.name: Climax volume
concept.definition: An extreme volume surge — typically the heaviest volume in many bars and several times the recent average — occurring after an extended directional move and accompanied by a wide price spread. In Wyckoff analysis it is the volume signature of a buying or selling climax: the terminal effort of a crowd capitulating or chasing.
concept.intuition: When everyone who was going to trade finally rushes in at once, the burst of activity can mark the end of a move rather than its acceleration.
concept.mechanics: Identified by comparing bar volume against the recent distribution of volumes together with spread expansion and location after a mature trend; practitioners then watch whether price can make further progress — failure to do so is what retrospectively confirms the climax.
concept.failure_modes: Climactic volume also occurs on genuine news repricing and on expiration or rebalance days, where it starts new trends rather than ending old ones; the label is dependable only in hindsight once the expected stalling appears.
concept.misconceptions: The highest-volume bar is not automatically a climax; climax interpretation requires context — a mature preceding move plus subsequent failure of price to continue.
concept.example: After a six-day selloff, a market prints its widest down bar on triple the 20-day average volume, closes well off the low, and cannot make a new low the next session — classic climax volume at a potential selling climax.
